newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korean won plummets to new low of 880.00.
newsitem.headline: South Korean won plummets to new low of 880.00.

text.p: The won fell to a new 84-month low of 880.00 against the U.S. dollar in late Monday afternoon trading, pressured by a widening trade deficit and the dollar's strength on world markets, dealers said.
This is the lowest level seen for the local currency since the market-average system was launched in March 1990.

Dealers said little impact was seen from heightening tension between North and South Korea. Tensions have flared up in the Korean peninsula after an attempted defection by a high-ranking North Korean official in Beijing last Wednesday and a weekend attack near Seoul on a high-profile Northern defector by suspected North Korean agents.

"I can't say that there is absolutely no impact from the problems between North and South Korea. But the recent rise is mostly due to speculative buying based on the dollar's strength and the trade deficit," said a western bank dealer. "Investors are convinced the dollar will just keep climbing."
Earlier supportive intervention by the central Bank of Korea hardly put a dent in the won's downward momentum, traders said.
The central bank has refused to confirm or deny that it intervenes in interbank trading.
